newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli warplanes strike after Lebanon blasts.
newsitem.headline: Israeli warplanes strike after Lebanon blasts.

text.p: Israeli warplanes attacked suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon on Sunday, hours after two members of an Israeli-backed militia were killed in bomb explosions.
Lebanese security sources said two Israeli warplanes fired four rockets in two rounds at 4:20 p.m. (1320 GMT) into hills northwest of Jizzine.
The Israeli army confirmed the air raid.
"Warplanes attacked terrorist targets in the Jizzine area this afternoon. Pilots reported accurate hits and all planes returned safely to base," a military announcement in Jerusalem said.
There was no immediate word on casualties.

Earlier pro-Israeli militia sources in south Lebanon said a captain in the South Lebanon Army militia was killed by a bomb planted in his car and another SLA militiaman died when a roadside bomb exploded as he rushed to the scene of the first attack.

In Beirut, the pro-Iranian Hizbollah claimed responsibility for both attacks which occured in Jizzine, a strip of territory officially outside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone but under SLA control.
Hizbollah guerrillas regularly attack Israeli troops and their local militia allies in a bid to oust them from the 15-km (nine miles)-wide occupation zone.
The pro-Israeli militia sources said the first blast occurred when 30-year-old SLA captain Asaad Nammour stepped into his car outside his house in the village of Bkassine.

The second blast took place as the jeep carrying the South Lebanon Army commander of Jizzine rushed to the scene of the earlier attack. A militiaman accompanying SLA commander Raymond Abu Mrad was killed. None of the other militiamen including the commander were hurt in the blast, the sources added.
The lastest bomb attacks brought to five the number of SLA militiamen killed in guerrilla attacks since the beginning of the year.

"The Islamic Resistance continues to hit hard with the aim of eliminating the remaining key agents following the instructions of the secretary general (Sheikh) Hassan Nasrallah," Hizbollah said in its statement.
Pro-Israeli militia sources said guerrillas fired mortar bombs into the outpost of Kassarat al-Oroush in the eastern sector of the zone.
In retaliation, Israeli gunners shelled south Lebanese areas facing the outpost. No casualties were reported in the shelling.
